Meridian Global at a glance

We map the world's markets so you can see the next deal first

Meridian Global is a global market intelligence firm. We map markets, regions, industries, deals, opportunities and risks, and startup funding, score where opportunity and threat are building over the short, medium and long term, and provide research and advisory support so you can act with confidence.

Who we are

An independent market-intelligence and research firm, based in India and serving clients globally. Every figure we publish names its source and date.

What we do

We map six layers: markets, regions, industries, deals, opportunities and risks, and startup funding, and turn them into clear outlooks across three time horizons.

How we help

Free research and tools, custom briefs, research retainers and advisory support: target screening, investor and buyer mapping, and round strategy.

      Deep dive · Renewable energy

      Record build-out, capital rotating to storage and grids

      Our latest read of the renewables market for deal teams: how fast capacity is growing, where the money is going, and what that means for M&A over the short, medium and long run.

      Renewables added, 2025692 GWA record year. Solar was 511 GW of it.
      Share of global power capacity49%5.14 TW of renewables installed at end-2025.
      Clean energy investment, 2026e$2.2TVersus about $1.2T for oil, gas and coal.
      Renewables M&A, H1 2026$64B▲ 20% versus $53B in H1 2025.

      Renewables deal flow by region · H1 2026

      North AmericaMost active

      About 85% of global deal value. Storage M&A up 70%. Private equity made 65% of acquisitions.

      Largest deal: $33.4B take-private of AES
      EuropeShifting to storage

      Record 69 battery storage deals (18 GW), double last year. Wind steady; solar deals down about 15%.

      Largest deal: CIP buys Ørsted's European onshore platform ($1.7B)
      APACGrowing

      Solar deals up about 70% and wind up 80%. India saw 21 solar deals covering 3.5 GW.

      Australia: most solar deals now include batteries
      LATAMSlowing

      Deal flow down about 70% year on year as investors wait for policy and currency clarity.

      Anchor deal: CPP's $1.7B investment in Inkia, Peru

      Opportunities

      • Storage and grids. Grid spending is near $550B and battery storage above $100B in 2026. Short to medium run.
      • Operating, contracted assets. About 80% of deals target late-stage or operating projects, so well-contracted portfolios command premiums. Short run.
      • Discounted listed funds. Listed renewable funds trade 25–40% below asset value, creating take-private and secondary deals. Short run.
      • Emerging growth markets. New capacity grew 28.9% in the Middle East and 15.9% in Africa in 2025, the fastest on record for both. Medium to long run.

      Threats

      • Merchant revenue risk. Battery revenues in Texas (ERCOT) fell 37% in 2025, so uncontracted assets face price pressure. Short run.
      • Fossil competition for capital. Gas investment is at a decade high and coal the highest since 2012. Renewables' share of new capacity slipped to 85.6% from 92.5%. Medium run.
      • Supply and security shocks. Middle East shipping disruption and tight turbine supply raise costs and delay projects. Short to medium run.
      • Policy and trade shifts. Subsidy changes and tariffs can reprice pipelines quickly, especially in the US and Latin America. Medium run.

      Sources: IRENA Renewable Capacity Statistics 2026 (2025 additions and installed capacity); IEA World Energy Investment 2026 (2026 estimates); Enerdatics Renewables M&A Outlook H1 2026 (deal flow). Opportunities and threats are Meridian Global's views, for information only and not investment advice. Data as of October 2026.

        Big decisions are still made on incomplete pictures.

        70–90%

        is the M&A failure rate that research commonly reports.

        Harvard Business Review, 2011 ↗
        ~60%

        of executives blamed deal failure on due diligence that missed critical issues.

        Bain & Company, 2020 ↗
        61%

        of managers say most of their decision-making time is used ineffectively.

        McKinsey, 2019 ↗
        17%

        of business buyers' purchase time is spent with suppliers; the rest is their own research.

        Gartner, 2020 ↗

        So we built it the other way round: open, sourced research you can check yourself, scored for what matters to a transaction, and a team that turns it into a clear answer when the stakes are high.

        Methodology

        How We Score the Deal Outlook

        Every score on this site follows the same process, so you can see how we reach a view and judge it for yourself.

        ▼▼−2Strong threat
        ▼−1Threat
        –0Neutral
        ▲+1Opportunity
        ▲▲+2Strong opportunity

        Three Lenses

        • By Sector: 8 industry groups
        • By Factor: Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Environmental, Legal
        • By Transaction: M&A, ECM, DCM, Leveraged Finance, Restructuring

        Three Horizons

        • 0–12 months: catalysts, rates, deal pipelines
        • 1–3 years: policy, capital flows, sector cycles
        • 3–10 years: structural themes: energy, AI, demographics

        What a Score Means

        Expected effect on deal value, volume and execution risk for that region and horizon. For Restructuring, a higher score means more distressed situations.

        1. CollectOfficial data (IMF, World Bank, central banks), deal data (Mergermarket, LSEG, Dealogic), and bank and asset-manager research.
        2. SignalIdentify what is changing: policy, prices, capital flows, conflicts and regulation.
        3. ScoreAnalyst judgement on a −2 to +2 scale, cross-checked across lenses and regions.
        4. ReviewMonthly refresh, plus immediate updates when an event moves markets.
        5. PublishEach score shows its key number, reasoning, what to watch and sources.

        Scores are Meridian Global's views, not investment advice. They rely on public data, which can lag events; some paywalled sources are not used.

        FAQ

        Questions, answered

        Quick, straight answers about our research, our data, our startup tools and how to work with us.

        About usWhat does Meridian Global do?

        We provide deal-focused global market intelligence: daily market data, outlooks by region, industry and deal type, researched Insights, research and advisory support, and funding tools for startups.

        About usWho is it for?

        Corporates and deal teams, private equity and venture funds, family offices, sovereign and institutional investors, advisers, incubators and founders. See Who We Serve.

        About usDo you raise capital or execute transactions?

        No. We provide research and advisory support. Securities offerings and financing are arranged by regulated banks and lenders.

        About usIs this investment advice?

        No. Our content is general information only and does not constitute investment, legal or tax advice. Talk to a regulated adviser before making decisions.

        Research & dataWhere does your data come from?

        Every figure on the site names its source and date: official bodies (IMF, World Bank, central banks), deal data (Mergermarket, LSEG, Dealogic, PitchBook), and research from banks, law firms and industry bodies. Our own views are labelled as such.

        Research & dataHow often is the research updated?

        Live Market updates daily, every trading day. Industry Coverage and Deal Coverage are updated weekly, every Monday. Each section shows a Last updated stamp. Outlook scores are reviewed monthly, and sooner when a major event moves markets.

        Research & dataWhy do your figures sometimes differ from other sources?

        Data providers count deals differently, so totals can differ. Where they disagree, we show both and say why. For example, Mergermarket puts global M&A for Jan–Sep 2026 at $4.44tn while LSEG counts $3.9tn.

        Research & dataHow are the outlook scores made?

        We score each area from −2 (strong threat) to +2 (strong opportunity) over three horizons, 0–12 months, 1–3 years and 3–10 years, using official data, deal data and institutional research. See our Methodology.

        Research & dataDo you publish your mistakes?

        Yes. Our Track Record logs every call with its date, each revision and what happened next, including misses.

        Research & dataWhat do you cover?

        6 regions, 8 industry groups and 5 deal types (M&A, ECM, DCM, leveraged finance and restructuring), plus country fact sheets for 24 markets.

        StartupsAre the founder templates free?

        Yes. Join our mailing list once to unlock all nine templates in the Founder Toolkit. They are general starting points; details vary by business and region, so talk to our team for advice on your situation.

        StartupsCan you help us raise a round?

        We provide advisory support: investor long-lists, valuation ranges from comparable rounds, round strategy and plain-English term-sheet notes. We are not a broker and cannot guarantee an outcome. See Raise Capital.

        StartupsDo you help with grants and accelerators?

        Yes. The Funding Finder covers 95 programmes with deadlines, and we offer application reviews.

        StartupsWhich countries do your startup guides cover?

        Our Raise in… guides cover India, the United States, the United Kingdom, the European Union, the UAE, Saudi Arabia and Singapore.

        Working with usHow do I request a custom brief?

        Use the contact form: choose your interest, tell us what you are working on and how you would like to be contacted. We reply with a proposed scope.

        Working with usHow quickly will you reply?

        We aim to reply within two working days with an outline of how we can help.

        Working with usWhat does it cost?

        The website, the Meridian Briefing and the founder templates are free. Custom briefs, research retainers and advisory support are scoped and priced per engagement. See How to Work With Us.

        Working with usCan we share confidential information?

        Yes. Everything you share is treated as confidential and used only to respond to you. If you need an NDA before sharing sensitive details, tell us in your enquiry.

        Working with usIs the Meridian Briefing free?

        Yes. It is a monthly email with our outlook and new Insights, plus alerts only when markets move. Subscribe here.

        PrivacyHow do you handle my data?

        We only use your details to respond to you or send what you asked for. We never sell your data. See our Privacy Policy.

        PrivacyHow do I unsubscribe?

        Every email includes an unsubscribe link, or contact us and we will remove you.
